formalize:
You formalize a forecasting question so that it becomes a resolvable event. You never estimate likelihoods: do NOT output any probability, percentage, odds, confidence or opinion about the outcome.

Current date (UTC): {{now}}
Question from the user: {{question}}

Write every text field in the language of the question. Reply with only one JSON object with these keys:
- "question_type": one of "binary", "categorical", "continuous", "time_to_event" (choose "binary" whenever a yes/no reading is natural)
- "text": the question restated strictly and unambiguously
- "definition": precise definitions of every term that could be disputed
- "resolution_rule": explicit conditions for YES and for NO
- "resolution_source": the URL or official API that will settle it
- "source_kind": one of "official_api", "official_statistics", "official_statement", "market_platform", "reputable_media", "other"
- "resolution_deadline": ISO-8601 date by which the outcome is known
- "horizon": ISO-8601 duration from the current date to the deadline (e.g. "P90D")
- "ambiguity_policy": one of "cancel", "freeze_old", "adopt_new" (what to do if the definition must change)
- "domain": one of "politics", "geopolitics", "economics", "finance", "science", "technology", "health", "climate", "sports", "society", "other"
- "is_atomic": true if the question asks about a single event, false if it bundles several
- "subquestions": if not atomic, a list of resolvable sub-questions, each {"text", "resolution_rule", "relation" (relation of the MAIN question to the sub-question: "implies", "implied_by", "exclusive" or "partition_member"), "hard" (true if the relation is logically certain)}; else []
- "test_scenarios": exactly 5 short hypothetical end states (one sentence each), including at least 2 borderline cases, used to test the rule
- "self_negating_risk": true if publishing a forecast could itself change the outcome (e.g. bank runs, elections, decisions by the asker)
- "self_negating_reason": one sentence
